figures.caption:
For $p=3$, the normalized child characters
contain one average and two orthogonal complex details. Solid curves
show real parts and dashed curves show imaginary parts. The level
rank $(p-1)p^{r-1}$ grows by the branching factor. The atlas uses
$\mathsf F_r$ for the corresponding infinite cylinder detail; its
finite restriction is $D_r^{(h)}$ for $r\leq h$.

A finite compatible Hamiltonian has
zero blocks between its embedded coarse space and its new detail
space. In the plotted example, adding an off-diagonal coupling creates
detail probability from a coarse initial state. This finite example
illustrates the block criterion and supplies a negative control for
unconditional refinement claims.

Three exact folded bands for the
nearest-neighbor cycle. The discrete markers represent the finite cyclic
spectrum. Band folding reorganizes its multiplicities without discarding
any eigenstate.

A branch-normalized finite tree has
the same root response as its radial Jacobi chain. The complex-energy
resolvent avoids real poles. The oscillatory memory is the return
amplitude of a finite hidden chain.

The normalized maps
$R_2$, $R_3$, and $R_5$ preserve the same arcsine spectral measure.
The accompanying bounded moment checks illustrate the exact measure
identity, while each Schur realization retains its own excluded poles.

Exact infinite tails for the geometric
level masses of Example \ref{a-limit-geometric-example}. The operator
domain controls a weighted tail in addition to the state norm tail.
The parameters are declared in the plate and its reproducible Python
source.

A finite cycle--tree walk, aggregated over
vertices at the same tree depth. The graph-distance support check uses
the full product graph, including prefix labels. Probability plotted
against depth alone displays only an aggregation of that geometry.
